entries.description:
What every element of a form's `Controls` has — gathered here once rather than repeated under each control. It is not a type a script names: a script holds a Button, a Textctrl, a Tablebox, and each of them answers to these members as well as its own.

A control's members are its PROPERTIES, the same ones the designer's inspector shows, under the same names. A script reads them and sets them while the form is open, and the client draws the control anew in the next frame. Every control has Name, FunctionalOptions and Events. Every control that is a window — all but the sizers, the notebook page and the table's columns and column groups — also has MinimumSize, MaximumSize, Font, ForegroundColour, BackgroundColour, Tooltip, Enabled and Visible. A control that stands in a sizer has the sizer item's properties too (Proportion, Stretch, the border ones — see SizerItem).

A control is reached as `Controls.<Name>` (or `Controls.FindControl(name)`). `ThisForm.<Name>` gives the control's VALUE when it holds one (a field, a checkbox, a table), and the control itself otherwise.
entries.syntax_block:
Controls.Field1.Visible = False;
Controls.Field1.Tooltip = "Filled in by the system";
entries.example:
Controls.Comment.Enabled = Not ThisForm.ReadOnly;
Controls.Total.ForegroundColour = New Colour(200, 0, 0);

entries.description: The control's name: what `Controls.<Name>`, `Controls.FindControl` and `ThisForm.<Name>` find it by, and what the designer shows in the form's tree. Unique on the form. Read it from a script; give it in the designer — a name changed while the form is open is not checked against the others, and the form's lists keep knowing the control by the name it opened with.

The functional options the control is available under: while every one of them is off, the control is neither shown nor offered, and neither is what it holds. Empty — available whatever the options say. It works beside Visible and does not change it. Chosen in the designer; a script can read it, but assigning it changes nothing.

The control's events, by name — what the control calls when something happens in it (a field's OnChange, a table's Selection). Read-only as a property; the events in it are set: a named form procedure (`New Event("Name")`) or a function value written in place. Which events a control has is said in its own article; a button has none, it runs a command.

The smallest size the form's layout may give the control, in pixels; -1 on a side means no limit there. The layout never shrinks the control below it, even when the form is made smaller. A sizer has a MinimumSize of its own, for the area it lays out.
The largest size the form's layout may give the control, in pixels; -1 on a side means no limit there. Keeps a stretched field from growing across a wide form.

The control's font. Unset, the parent's font is used, and a font set on a group or a page is inherited by the controls inside it that have no font of their own. A Font value assigned from a script is drawn in the next frame; anything that is not a Font is ignored.

The colour of the control's text. By default the system colour, which follows the user's theme — set it only where the colour says something (a sum gone negative), not to decorate. A value that is not a Colour is ignored.
The colour behind the control. By default the system colour, which follows the user's theme; a field's default is the theme's field background. A value that is not a Colour is ignored.

The text shown when the mouse pointer rests over the control; empty — no tooltip. It is written per language: a script reads and writes the text of the session's language, and the other languages keep theirs.
entries.example: Controls.Rate.Tooltip = "Taken from the price list of " + String(Object.PriceDate);

entries.description: Whether the user can work with the control. A disabled control is shown greyed out and takes no input; disabling a group or a page disables everything inside it. What the client gets is this AND the form's own Enabled: a control on a disabled form is disabled whatever it says.

Whether the control is shown. A hidden control keeps its data and can be shown again from code; the layout closes the gap it leaves. What the client gets is this AND the control's availability: a control whose functional options are all off, or a field with no source picked, stays hidden whatever Visible says.

The place a control takes in its sizer: how much of the spare room it gets, whether it stretches across, and the margin kept around it. A script never holds a sizer item on its own — `Controls` skips them — but every control that stands in a sizer has these properties as its own: `Controls.Comment.Proportion = 1;`. Set while the form is open, they lay the form out again in the next frame.

How much of its sizer's spare room the control takes along the sizer's direction. 0, the default, keeps its natural size. Otherwise the spare room is shared in these proportions: controls with 1 and 2 get one third and two thirds of it.
entries.example: Controls.Comment.Proportion = 1;   // takes what is left of the height

entries.description: The control's size ACROSS its sizer's direction. WindowStretch.Shrink, the default: its natural size. WindowStretch.Expand: the full width of a vertical sizer, or the full height of a horizontal one.
The empty margin kept around the control, in pixels, on the sides switched on by BorderLeft, BorderRight, BorderTop and BorderBottom. Default 5.
Whether the margin of BorderSize is kept on the control's left side. On by default.
Whether the margin of BorderSize is kept on the control's right side. On by default.
Whether the margin of BorderSize is kept above the control. On by default.
Whether the margin of BorderSize is kept below the control. On by default.

A button on a form. A press runs its COMMAND — a form command, a standard command of the form or of one of its tables, or a command of the configuration; a button has no click event of its own, the code goes into the command's handler (its Action).

Its own properties: View (a button or a hyperlink), Title, Representation (text, picture or both), Picture, PictureLocation, Note (the line under a tile) and Command. It also has what every window control has (see Control) and, in a sizer, the sizer item's properties.
entries.example:
Controls.Post.Enabled = Not Object.Posted;
Controls.Post.Title = "Post and close";

entries.description: How the button is drawn: ButtonView.Button, with a face and a frame, or ButtonView.Hyperlink — no face and no frame, its caption underlined. Pressed the same way either way; its picture and its command do not change.

The text on the button. Written per language: a script reads and writes the text of the session's language. Empty, the button shows the caption of its command. Whether the text is shown at all is Representation's to say.

What the button shows: Representation.Text, .Picture or .PictureAndText. Representation.Auto, the default: what the bound command prefers (Close is a picture alone, Add a picture with text), and a picture with text when no command is bound.
The button's icon, beside or instead of the text (see Representation and PictureLocation). A script reads it as a picture value and may assign another one; a value that is not a picture is ignored.

Where the picture stands: PictureLocation.Auto (where the button puts it, on the left of the text), .Left, .Right, or .Tile — the picture large over the text and the Note under them, the button filling what its sizer gives it: a big button for a finger.
The line under a tile's title — a price, a count, a state. Shown only when PictureLocation is Tile. Written per language, and changed from code while the form is open like the title.

The command a press runs: a form command, a standard command of the form or of one of its tables, or a command of the configuration. It is chosen in the designer and is no script value: a script can neither read nor set it — to change what a press does, change the command's handler, or show another button.

An input field: it shows and edits one value — a form attribute, a field of the form's object, or a field reached from them by a dotted path (read-only). The value's type decides how typed text is parsed and which choice form the Select button opens.

Its own properties: Value, Title, Source, the editing modes (PasswordMode, MultilineMode, TexteditMode), Format, the choice settings (ChoiceForm, QuickChoice, ChoiceFoldersAndItems, TypeLink, ChoiceParameters) and its buttons (ButtonSelect, ButtonClear, ButtonOpen); and what every window control has (see Control).

Its events, set through Events: OnChange, StartChoice, StartListChoice, Clearing, Opening, ChoiceProcessing.

The value in the field. Read, it is the value of the bound source (an attribute, a field of it). Written, the value is first fitted to the field's link by type and to its type, then written into the source when the binding is direct — a field reached through a reference is read-only, and the write leaves it as it was; the fields chosen within this one are emptied on a change, and the form is drawn again. A field with no source keeps the value for itself.
The field's caption, shown beside it. Empty: the bound field's synonym. Written per language: a script reads and writes the text of the session's language.

What the field is bound to, as the dotted path it is read by: `"Object.Partner"`, `"Filter"`, `"Object.Partner.Region"`. A script reads the path and may bind the field anew by writing one; an empty string unbinds, and a path that does not resolve raises rather than leaving the field showing what it showed. A path through a reference is read-only. A field with no source is not shown.
entries.return_descr: String — the path, empty when unbound.

entries.description: Whether the field hides what is typed behind placeholder characters, for a secret such as a password. Off by default.
Whether the field takes several lines of text (Enter starts a new line) — for comments and addresses. Off by default: Enter finishes the input.
Whether the value can be typed into the field. Off: it can only be picked with the Select button or cleared. On by default; a field bound through a reference path is read-only whatever this says.
entries.example: Controls.Partner.TexteditMode = False;   // only chosen from the list

entries.description: How the field shows its value — digits after the point, separators, a date pattern. Written per language. Empty: the bound attribute's format, and without one a number shows as many digits after the point as its type keeps.

Which form opens when the user presses Select: one of the forms of the value's type. Empty: the type's default choice form. Chosen in the designer from the forms the type has; what a script reads is the chosen entry, and a value that is not one of those entries is not taken.
entries.return_descr: The chosen form, or nothing when the default is used.

entries.description: How a reference is picked into the field when Select is pressed. QuickChoiceMode.Auto: as its type says (the catalog's or the document's own Quick choice). .Use: a drop-down of the matching items. .DontUse: the list form.

For a field referring to a hierarchical catalog: what may be picked into it — ChoiceFoldersAndItems.Items, .Folders or .FoldersAndItems. ChoiceFoldersAndItems.Auto: what the bound attribute's own setting says.

The field whose value decides the TYPE of a value written into this one: a characteristic gives the type it declares, a field holding a type description gives that, any other field gives the type of the value standing in it. Set in the designer; a script reads the path of that field as a string and cannot assign it.
entries.return_descr: String — the path of the linked field, empty when there is none.

entries.description: What the list shows when a reference is chosen into the field, on top of what the bound field declares itself: a row per parameter — which field of the chosen object it filters, which field the form reaches gives the value, and what becomes of a chosen value when that field changes. Set in the designer; a script reads their names as a string and cannot assign them.
Whether the field shows the Select button (...), which opens a choice form or a list to pick the value from. On by default.
Whether the field shows the Clear button (X), which empties the value. On by default.
entries.example: Controls.Partner.ButtonClear = False;   // a partner is required

entries.description: Whether the field shows the Open button, which opens the form of the referenced object. Off by default.

A checkbox: it shows and toggles one boolean value — a form attribute or a field of the form's object. Bound through a reference path, or on a view-only form, it shows the value but cannot be toggled; with no source it is not shown at run time.

Its own properties: Value, Title, TitleLocation and Source; and what every window control has (see Control). Its event, set through Events: OnCheckboxClicked.

Whether the box is checked. Read, it is the value of the bound source; written, it goes into the source when the binding is direct (one through a reference is read-only) and the box shows it in the next frame.
The checkbox's caption. Empty: the bound field's synonym. Written per language: a script reads and writes the text of the session's language.
Which side of the box the caption sits on: TitleLocation.Left (the default) or TitleLocation.Right.

The boolean value the checkbox is bound to, as the dotted path it is read by (`"Object.Active"`). A script reads the path and may bind the box anew by writing one; an empty string unbinds, and a path that does not resolve raises.
entries.return_descr: String — the path, empty when unbound.

entries.description: A radio button. It has no data source and no event: its own properties are Title and Selected, and it has what every window control has (see Control). The form does not hear the user clicking it — Selected says what was set, by the designer or by code, not what the user picked; for a choice the form must know, bind a field or a checkbox to an attribute instead.
The radio button's caption. Written per language: a script reads and writes the text of the session's language.
Whether the radio button is shown selected. Set from code, it is drawn in the next frame. A click on the client is not read back into it.

A caption on a form. Unbound, it is plain text. Bound to a value (Source), it shows that value beside the caption, and a non-empty value is drawn as a link that opens its own form.

Its own properties: Title, TitleLocation, Source, and two kept for older forms (Markup, Wrap); and what every window control has (see Control). Its event, set through Events: Opening — the link was clicked; turning StandardProcessing off keeps the form from opening.

The caption's text. Empty on a bound static text: the bound field's synonym. Written per language: a script reads and writes the text of the session's language. For several lines put line breaks into the text.
Which side of the value the caption sits on when the static text is bound: TitleLocation.Left (the default) or TitleLocation.Right.

Optional: the value shown beside the caption — a form attribute or any field reached from it by a dotted path — as the path it is read by. A script reads the path and may set another; an empty string makes the static text a plain caption again, and a path that does not resolve raises.
entries.return_descr: String — the path, empty when unbound.

entries.description: Kept for older forms and saved with the form; it has no effect — the caption is always shown as plain text.
entries.example:
// no effect: the caption is plain text either way
Controls.Hint.Markup = False;

entries.description: Kept for older forms and saved with the form; it has no effect. For several lines, put line breaks into the title.
A separating line. Its own property is Orient; it has what every window control has (see Control). For the line to run the full width or height, set its Stretch to WindowStretch.Expand.
The line's direction: WindowOrient.Horizontal (the default), separating stacked parts of a form, or WindowOrient.Vertical, separating side-by-side ones.

A progress bar. Its own properties are Range, Value and Orient; it has what every window control has (see Control). Code moves it by setting Value; it is drawn in the next frame the form sends, so a long loop in one call shows only where it ended.
The value at which the bar is full. Default 100, so Value reads as a percentage.
How far the bar is filled, from 0 to Range. Default 30.
The bar's direction: WindowOrient.Horizontal (the default, filling left to right) or WindowOrient.Vertical.

A slider with a thumb. Its own properties are MinValue, MaxValue, Value and Orient; it has what every window control has (see Control). It has no source and no event, and the form does not hear the user dragging it: Value says where code put the thumb, not where the user left it.
The slider's smallest value, at its start. Default 0.
The slider's largest value, at its end. Default 100.
Where the thumb stands, between MinValue and MaxValue. Default 50. Set from code, it is drawn in the next frame; a drag on the client is not read back into it.
The slider's direction: WindowOrient.Horizontal (the default) or WindowOrient.Vertical.

A table on a form: it shows a list — a dynamic list, a value table or tree, or a tabular section of the form's object — row by row, its columns (TableboxColumn, TableboxColumnGroup) bound to the list's fields, and carries a command bar with the list's commands.

Its own properties: Value (the list), CurrentRow, Source, Header, HeaderHeight, Footer, FooterHeight, FrezeeRow, FrezeeCol, RowSelectionMode, ViewMode and ChoiceMode; and what every window control has (see Control). Its events, set through Events: Selection (the current row changes), OnActivateRow (double click or Enter), BeforeAddRow, BeforeDeleteRow, OnAddRow, OnDeleteRow. A column's own events (OnChange, StartChoice and the rest) are the column's.

The list the table shows: a Table, a dynamic list, a tabular section. Assigning another list shows it instead — the current row is dropped, and a list that makes its own columns (a Table filled by code) gets them made anew. To bind the table to another form attribute for good, set Source.

The row the cursor stands on — a row of the list the table shows, or Undefined when there is none. Assigned, it moves the cursor: a row of this table's list, or what stands for a row — a reference of a dynamic list's row, a value of a row; anything that is not one of its rows leaves the table with no current row.
entries.return_descr: A row of the list, or Undefined.

entries.description: The form attribute the table shows, as the path it is read by: a dynamic list, a value table or tree, or a tabular section of the form's object (`"Object.Goods"`). Written at run time, it is a new table: the list and its columns are made anew. An empty string unbinds; a path that does not resolve raises.
entries.return_descr: String — the path, empty when unbound.

entries.description: Whether the column headers are shown above the rows. On by default; clicking a header sorts by that column.
The header's height in text lines. At least 1, and never less than the column groups need, so a grouped header always fits.
Whether a footer row is shown under the rows, carrying each column's FooterText — a total, for example. Off by default.
The footer's height in text lines, used when the footer is shown. Default 1.
How many leading rows stay in place while the rest scroll vertically. 0, the default: none. The name is spelled so — FrezeeRow — and a script writes it that way.
How many leading columns stay in place while the rest scroll horizontally — keeps a name column in view in a wide table. 0, the default: none. Spelled FrezeeCol.

What the cursor highlights. TableboxRowSelectionMode.SelectCell, the default: one cell, moved cell by cell — suits a table edited in place. .SelectRow: the whole row — suits a list rows are picked or opened from.

How a list with folders or parents is shown. TableboxViewMode.Hierarchical, the default: one level at a time, entering a folder to see what is in it. .Tree: an expandable tree. .List: every row flat, the hierarchy ignored.

Whether the table works as a picker: a double click or Enter hands the current row back to whoever opened the form instead of opening or editing it, and a Select command leads its command bar. Set by itself on a choice form's list.

A column of a table: it shows and edits one field of the table's list. It is an element of `Controls` like any other, by its own name. A column is not a window: of the shared members it has Name, FunctionalOptions and Events; it is hidden and shown by its own Visible.

Its own properties: Title, Source, Width, Visible, the editing modes (PasswordMode, MultilineMode, TexteditMode), Format, the footer (FooterText, FooterAlign, FooterPicture), the header (HeaderAlign, HeaderPicture, Representation), Resizable, Reorderable, the choice settings (ChoiceForm, QuickChoice, ChoiceFoldersAndItems, TypeLink, ChoiceParameters) and the cell editor's buttons (ButtonSelect, ButtonClear, ButtonOpen). Its events, set through Events: OnChange, StartChoice, StartListChoice, Clearing, Opening, ChoiceProcessing.
The column's header text. Empty: the synonym of the bound field, or the column's name when nothing is bound. Written per language: a script reads and writes the text of the session's language.

The field of the table's list this column shows and edits, as the path it is read by. A path through a reference (such as `Owner.Description`) is shown read-only. A script reads the path and may set another; an empty string unbinds, and a path that does not resolve raises.
entries.return_descr: String — the path, empty when unbound.

entries.description: The column's starting width, in pixels. The user can change it when the column is Resizable.
Whether the column is shown. A hidden column keeps its data and can be shown again from code.
Whether the cell editor hides what is typed behind placeholder characters, for a secret such as a password. Off by default.
Whether the cell editor takes several lines of text (Enter starts a new line). Off by default: Enter finishes the edit.
Whether the value can be typed into the cell. Off: it can only be picked with the Select button or cleared. On by default; a read-only column never takes typing.

How the column shows its cells — digits after the point, separators, a date pattern. Written per language. Empty: the bound attribute's format, and without one a number shows as many digits after the point as its type keeps.
The text in this column's footer cell, shown when the table's Footer is on — a label, or a total set from code. Written per language.
How the footer text is aligned: WindowHorizontalAlignment.Left (the default), .Center or .Right. Right suits a total under a numeric column.
An icon in the column's footer cell, beside or instead of the footer text (see Representation). A value that is not a picture is ignored.
How the header text is aligned: WindowHorizontalAlignment.Left (the default), .Center or .Right.
An icon in the column's header cell, beside or instead of the title (see Representation). A narrow flag column often shows only a picture.
What the header and footer cells show: Representation.Text, .Picture or .PictureAndText. Representation.Auto: the title and the picture, whichever are set.
Whether the user can change the column's width by dragging the edge of its header. On by default.
Whether the user can move the column to another place by dragging its header. On by default.
Which form opens when the user presses Select in the cell: one of the forms of the value's type. Empty: the type's default choice form. Chosen in the designer from the forms the type has.
entries.return_descr: The chosen form, or nothing when the default is used.

entries.description: How a reference is picked into the cell when Select is pressed. QuickChoiceMode.Auto: as its type says. .Use: a drop-down of the matching items. .DontUse: the list form.

For a column referring to a hierarchical catalog: what may be picked into its cells — ChoiceFoldersAndItems.Items, .Folders or .FoldersAndItems. ChoiceFoldersAndItems.Auto: what the bound attribute's own setting says.

The field whose value decides the TYPE of a value written into the column's cell: a characteristic gives the type it declares, a field holding a type description gives that, any other field gives the type of its value. Set in the designer; a script reads the path of that field and cannot assign it.
entries.return_descr: String — the path of the linked field, empty when there is none.

entries.description: What the list shows when a reference is chosen into the column's cell, on top of what the bound field declares itself: a row per parameter — which field of the chosen object it filters and which field the form reaches gives the value. Set in the designer; a script reads their names as a string and cannot assign them.
Whether the cell editor shows the Select button (...), which opens a choice form or a list to pick the value from. On by default.
Whether the cell editor shows the Clear button (X), which empties the value. On by default.
Whether the cell editor shows the Open button, which opens the form of the referenced object. Off by default.

A group of a table's columns: it arranges the columns inside it — stacked in one width, side by side under a title, or merged into one header cell — and groups nest. It is an element of `Controls` by its own name; it is not a window, and of the shared members it has Name, FunctionalOptions and Events.

Its own properties: Title, Grouping, ShowTitle, HeaderAlign and Visible.
entries.example: Controls.GoodsPrices.Visible = ShowPrices;   // the group's columns go with it

entries.description: The group's title in the header, shown when ShowTitle is on (an in-cell group always shows it, as its one header cell). Written per language.

Where the group's columns go. TableboxColumnGrouping.Vertical, the default: stacked within one width, so the row grows taller instead of wider. .Horizontal: side by side under the group's title. .InCell: side by side but merged under one header cell, reading as one field.
Whether the group's title takes a band of the header above its columns. Off, the default: the group only arranges its columns and costs the header no height.
How the group's title is aligned in its header cell: WindowHorizontalAlignment.Left, .Center (the default) or .Right.
Whether the group and all its columns are shown. Hidden columns keep their data and can be shown again from code.
